history.summary: A 2000 99-yr leasehold 2BR in West Coast (D05), an oversized 1,130 sqft at $1.258M / $1,113 psf with no nearby MRT. The headline-low PSF and 694 score are artefacts of the large unit and low quantum; a 26-year-old leasehold (~73 yrs left), no transit and a highly uncertain arena record (124 draws) make this a cautious hold at best.
history.rating_rationale: $1,113 psf looks cheap only because 1,130 sqft is oversized for a 2BR — quantum $1.258M is the real signal. 2000-built 99-yr LH means ~73 years of lease left (financing/decay drag building). No MRT within walking distance is a material liquidity handicap. The 143-157-124 record (huge draw count) flags very thin/uncertain data; D05 One-North/TEL tailwind is the main saving grace.
red_flags: No MRT within walking distance — weak connectivity in a transit-driven market
2000-built 99-yr leasehold — ~73 years remaining, lease-decay and financing drag
Low PSF is an oversized-unit artefact, not genuine value
Arena record dominated by draws (124) — unreliable/thin comparison data
catalysts: D05 One-North tech hub + Thomson-East Coast Line regional growth
Sub-$1.3M quantum keeps it in the deep-liquidity band
Spacious 1,130 sqft layout appeals to space-seeking families

history.summary: An aging 99-LH West Coast 2BR asking $1,113 psf — within the project's 12-month range ($922-$1,306, avg ~$1,155), so fairly priced but not a deep bargain. Accelerating lease decay (~68 yrs left) caps the forward case.
history.rating_rationale: Web checks resolve the dossier's data gaps: Westcove is a 99-yr-from-1995 development (~68 years remaining), and the 'very_low_psf' flag is real, not a mis-scrape — recent transactions average ~$1,155 psf. The asking $1,113 psf is slightly below that average but inside the normal band, so this is fair value rather than the cheap-vs-peers edge that v3.4 rewards. Critically, the dossier has 0 appreciation transactions and null cohort data, so the -20.6% age-adj 'cheap' signal is essentially unverified by the algo and I down-weight it. The forward drag is lease decay: a ~30-year-old 99-LH unit faces steepening depreciation, CPF-usage and financing restrictions tightening as it crosses key lease thresholds over a 5-7yr hold. Offsetting positives: West Coast/D5 is OCR (favorable fwd ~+4.0%), the estate is quiet and low-density near NUS/one-north with solid tenant demand, and the absolute quantum ($1.26M) is accessible. Net: fairly priced asset with real location merit but a structural lease headwind — a clean Neutral.
red_flags: 99-yr leasehold from 1995 — only ~68 years left; lease decay accelerates over the hold
0 appreciation txns and null cohort data — algo 'cheap' signal is unverified
Asking $1,113 psf is fair (within range) not a bargain vs ~$1,155 avg
catalysts: OCR/D5 location with favorable realized forward drift (~+4.0%)
Proximity to NUS, one-north and West Coast Highway supports rental demand
Accessible quantum (~$1.26M) widens the resale buyer pool
